introduction_markdown: Answer any FIVE out of the eight questions. If more than five questions are answered, only the first five will be marked. All questions carry equal marks. Marks allocated to parts of questions are indicated in brackets. Illustrate your answers wherever desirable with large, clear and fully labelled diagrams. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. Time allowed: three hours.
enonce_intro_markdown:
A cocoa farmer planted two species of cocoa plants. The cocoa plants with green and smooth pods were dominant over those with red and rough pods. A cross between a green and smooth pod cocoa plant and that with red and rough pod plant gave all the F$_1$ offspring having green and smooth pods. When the F$_1$ were allowed to cross with other cocoa plants with red and rough pods, the following results were obtained:

| Number | Phenotype |
|---|---|
| 380 | green and smooth pods cocoa plants |
| 63 | green and rough pods cocoa plants |
| 368 | red and rough pods cocoa plants |
| 69 | red and smooth pods cocoa plants |

Question 7 : calculs recalcules par script (total 880, parentaux 748, recombinants 132, valeur de crossing-over 15 pour cent, chi carre 431,6 pour l'hypothese 1:1:1:1, 0,47 pour 85:15). Les genotypes et le test-cross sont deduits de l'enonce (« other cocoa plants with red and rough pods » = double recessif).

questions.enonce_markdown: Use genetic symbols to illustrate these crosses. *[16 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Key.** $G$ = green pod (dominant), $g$ = red pod; $S$ = smooth pod (dominant), $s$ = rough pod.

**Observation.** The test cross does not give the 1 : 1 : 1 : 1 ratio expected for independent genes. The two **parental types** (green smooth 380 and red rough 368) are far more numerous than the two **recombinant types** (green rough 63 and red smooth 69), so the genes for pod colour and pod texture are **linked** on the same chromosome, with a few crossovers between them.

**Cross 1: the original parents (homozygous)**

| | |
|---|---|
| Parental phenotypes | green smooth $\times$ red rough |
| Parental genotypes | $\dfrac{GS}{GS}$ $\times$ $\dfrac{gs}{gs}$ |
| Gametes | all $GS$ ; all $gs$ |
| F$_1$ genotype | $\dfrac{GS}{gs}$ (heterozygous, $G$ and $S$ on the same chromosome) |
| F$_1$ phenotype | all **green and smooth** |

**Cross 2: test cross of the F$_1$ (with the double recessive, red rough)**

| | |
|---|---|
| Parental phenotypes | F$_1$ green smooth $\times$ red rough |
| Parental genotypes | $\dfrac{GS}{gs}$ $\times$ $\dfrac{gs}{gs}$ |
| Gametes of F$_1$ | **Parental (non-crossover):** $GS$ and $gs$ (large numbers). **Recombinant (crossover):** $Gs$ and $gS$ (few, made by crossing over at meiosis) |
| Gametes of the red rough plant | all $gs$ |

**Offspring (F$_2$ test-cross progeny)**

| Gamete from F$_1$ $\times$ $gs$ | Genotype | Phenotype | Number | Type |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| $GS$ | $\dfrac{GS}{gs}$ | green smooth | 380 | parental |
| $gs$ | $\dfrac{gs}{gs}$ | red rough | 368 | parental |
| $Gs$ | $\dfrac{Gs}{gs}$ | green rough | 63 | recombinant |
| $gS$ | $\dfrac{gS}{gs}$ | red smooth | 69 | recombinant |

Approximate expected result: about 42.5 per cent of each parental type and 7.5 per cent of each recombinant type (observed 43.2, 41.8, 7.2 and 7.8 per cent).

questions.enonce_markdown: Calculate the crossover value of the above crosses. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Crossover value (recombination frequency)** $= \dfrac{\text{number of recombinant (crossover) offspring}}{\text{total number of offspring}} \times 100$

- Recombinants (green rough + red smooth) $= 63 + 69 = 132$
- Total offspring $= 380 + 63 + 368 + 69 = 880$

$$\text{Crossover value} = \frac{132}{880} \times 100 = 15\%$$

(Check: parental types $= 380 + 368 = 748$, and $\frac{748}{880} \times 100 = 85\%$; $85\% + 15\% = 100\%$.)

**Crossover value = 15 per cent** (15 map units).

questions.enonce_markdown: What are the significances of this crossover value? *[2 marks]* *(16, 2, 2 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. It shows that the genes for pod colour and pod texture are **linked**, that is on the **same chromosome**, and that **crossing over** occurs between them (in 15 per cent of the gametes, so 85 per cent are parental types). Had they been on different chromosomes, the four classes would each be about 25 per cent (220 plants each), and a chi-squared test against this expectation ($\chi^2 \approx 432$, 3 degrees of freedom) rejects independent assortment.
2. Because the crossover value is proportional to the **distance** between genes, **1 per cent = 1 map unit**, so the two genes are **15 map units apart**. This value is used to **construct chromosome (linkage) maps** and locate genes relative to others.
3. It allows breeders to **predict the proportion of recombinant plants** from a cross (here 15 per cent), so they can plan how many plants to grow to obtain a desired new combination, such as green rough or red smooth pods.
